output.technical_predicate: Withdrawal of an optional consent (here: the "insights" purpose that generates repayment reports) must be as easy as giving it, must be preceded by information, and must stop future report generation — including jobs already queued and any retries — while leaving an unaffected subscriber's queued report deliverable.
applicability_facts: Scenario: two borrowers opt in (insights consent on) and queue reports; one withdraws before execution; the queue is reopened and drained twice; the other borrower remains eligible.

store.py:0092-0098 preference() accepts purpose 'insights' with value 'off' and, on that transition, cancels queued 'report' jobs for that owner's cases (UPDATE jobs SET state='cancelled' WHERE kind='report' AND state='queued' AND cid IN (SELECT id FROM cases WHERE owner=?)).
store.py:0137-0139 drain() executes a 'report' job only if enabled(db, c['owner'], 'insights') is still true, so a withdrawn owner's report cannot be generated on a later drain.
store.py:0088-0090 enabled() reads the latest choice row per (owner, purpose), so the withdrawal is the effective state for subsequent drains.
views.py:0033-0036 renders the privacy-choices section with the notice text and a single 'Switch off'/'Switch on' form per purpose, giving symmetric on/off controls.
store.py:0009 NOTICE states insights and promotions each require separate optional consent and can be switched off as easily as on, with withdrawal applying to future processing.
relevant_exceptions: No exception applies to the withdrawal itself; the requirement is that withdrawal stops future report generation.
The unaffected borrower's consent remains on, so their queued report is not covered by the withdrawal and may still be generated (store.py:0137-0139).
Restriction (restricted flag) is a separate control (store.py:0127-0128) and is not the withdrawal mechanism assessed here.
required_controls: Symmetric toggle: same form/route (/preference) and same effort to switch insights off as on (views.py:0034-0036; store.py:0092-0098).
Prior information: notice text describing optional separate consent and withdrawal before the toggle is shown (store.py:0009; views.py:0024-0025, 0033).
Cancellation of already-queued report jobs on withdrawal (store.py:0096-0098).
Execution-time re-check of consent so any re-queued or retried report is not generated after withdrawal (store.py:0137-0139 via enabled()).
Per-owner scoping so cancellation and the execution check affect only the withdrawing borrower's cases (store.py:0098, 0137).
assessment_limits: Assessment is static reading of the supplied source; no code was executed and no runtime behavior was observed.
The scenario's 'queue reopened and drained twice' is treated as a description of the test, not as evidence of execution; conclusions rest on the drain()/enabled() logic.
Retry semantics beyond re-draining queued jobs are not modeled in the source; only the queued-state cancellation and the execution-time consent check are assessed.
No assessment of other GDPR obligations (e.g., promotions/objection, erasure, portability) beyond their incidental appearance in the same functions.
Compliance is not decided from the rule text alone; it is inferred from the cited source coordinates under the stipulated scenario facts.
